Shophouse with 999-year leasehold tenure in Serangoon Garden up for sale at $10.8 mil
article:
A 999-year leasehold shophouse located in the Serangoon Garden area has been put up for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise.

The two-storey commercial property has a guide price of $10.8 million. This translates to $4,154 psf on its total built-up area of around 2,600 sq ft, which includes the five-foot way.

The ground floor of the shophouse is leased to an F&B establishment, while a fitness studio rents the upper floor. Altogether, the shophouse generates around $20,000 per month in rent, according to Neo Beng Lee of PropNex Shophouse Elites, a unit under PropNex Realty.

The property, located in the established Serangoon Garden landed estate, enjoys strong footfall, said Neo. “With no additional buyer’s stamp duty or GST applicable to the sale, and a limited supply of only 69 commercial shophouses in Serangoon Garden, we expect strong interest from both institutional and private investors — local and foreign alike,” he added.

The shophouse is part of a cluster of commercial properties in the Serangoon Garden area, comprising shophouses on Serangoon Garden Way, Maju Avenue and Kensington Park Road, along with retail mall myVillage. The cluster is also close to Chomp Chomp Food Centre and Serangoon Garden Market.

The latest shophouse transaction in the area was the sale of a 999-year leasehold property on a 2,146 sq ft site on Serangoon Garden Way in June. The two-storey shophouse, which is fully leased to Japanese restaurant Sushi Tei, fetched $15 million.

The transaction represents the highest sum paid for a single shophouse in Serangoon Garden estate , based on lodged caveats. It beat the previous high of $14.85 million set in December 2020 with the sale of another  999-year leasehold shophouse on Serangoon Garden Way.

However, the area’s biggest shophouse transaction by absolute sum was the sale of two adjoining shophouses on Serangoon Garden Way for $17.49 million in May 2023. The 999-year leasehold properties occup y a total land area of 3,101 sq ft.

The EOI will close at 3pm on Oct 16.

END

title: JLL appoints Mikhail Jaura as Apac head of data centre research
article:
JLL has announced the appointment of Mikhail Jaura as head of data centre research for Asia Pacific (Apac). The role is based in Hong Kong.

His appointment comes as the region continues to attract significant investment in data centre infrastructure, said Andrew Batson, global head of data centre research and strategy at JLL.

According to the firm, the global data centre sector is experiencing an unprecedented US$3 trillion ($3.8 trillion) infrastructure investment “supercycle”, driven by AI and hyperscale cloud services.

Jaura joins JLL from global technology intelligence firm International Data Corporation (IDC), where he served as senior research analyst for its Apac data centre research practice.

During his time at IDC, Jaura was responsible for consulting, recurring advisory services and regional business development.

He also launched IDC's Worldwide Semi-annual Datacenter Facilities Tracker, which measures capacity, emissions and non-IT capital expenditure across global hyperscale, colocation and enterprise footprints.

title: Batam to get its first Hilton Garden Inn in 2028
article:
Global hospitality company Hilton is set to open its first Hilton Garden Inn in Batam, Indonesia. The 199-key Hilton Garden Inn Batam City Centre will welcome guests in 2028. Hilton will manage the property, which is being developed by Indonesian company Sabang Raya Investama.

The hotel will be positioned to capture growing demand from corporate travel, meetings and events, weekend leisure visits, golf and wellness tourism, and medical-related stays, said Hilton in a September release.

“Batam continues to grow as an important business and leisure destination, supported by its close proximity to Singapore and Malaysia, strong connectivity and expanding visitor economy,” added Maria Ariizumi, Hilton’s vice-president, development for Southeast Asia and Australasia.

The hotel will be located in the heart of Batam, with convenient access to major commercial, retail and administrative hubs such as Lubuk Baja, Batam Cent re, and Hang Nadim International Airport.

It features standard rooms, family rooms and suites, along with amenities that include an all-day dining restaurant, bar, fitness centre, swimming pool, ballroom, and meeting rooms.

Hilton currently has 18 trading hotels in Indonesia, with another 16 in the pipeline.

title: New initiatives to boost quantity surveying profession, strengthen qualified persons' regulatory competencies
article:
The government has unveiled new initiatives to strengthen Singapore’s built environment, including recommendations to improve the quantity surveying industry and lift professional standards for qualified persons (QPs).

The initiatives were announced by Second Minister for Finance and National Development Indranee Rajah at the International Built Environment Week 2026 Industry & Awards Dinner on Sept 4.

During the event, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) also conferred awards recognising outstanding achievements in Singapore's built environment.

Push for more quantity surveyor talent, professional accreditation

Recommendations to strengthen the quantity surveying industry follow a six-month engagement period conducted by the Quantity Surveyors Workgroup with over 80 industry stakeholders.

The workgroup has recommended initiatives structured around three priorities: attracting talent, developing and retaining professionals, and enhancing the business sustainability of quantity surveying firms.

To attract talent, recommendations include introducing new quantity surveying content in the curriculum at institutes of higher learning, as part of a move to raise students’ awareness of the profession. Quantity surveying firms will also be onboarded onto Inspire, the government’s internship programme for students in built environment courses.

To develop and retain quantity surveying professionals, the workgroup has recommended the wider use of professional accreditation, such as the Accredited Professional Quantity Surveyor scheme.  In addition, the roles and responsibilities of quantity surveyors are proposed to be formally recognised in standard construction contracts, along with the adoption of competency-based remuneration to support career progression.

To support the business sustainability of quantity surveying firms, the workgroup recommends leveraging technology and AI to streamline workflows and processes. It also proposes the development of a framework to define the various quantity surveying services delivered at each project stage, which could help foster a more transparent and equitable procurement environment.

Strengthening regulatory competency for QPs

The government is also rolling out initiatives aimed at helping QPs — professionals licensed to prepare, submit and endorse building and structural plans for construction projects — continually upgrade their capabilities.

According to BCA, the Board of Architects and the Professional Engineers Board, together with regulatory agencies, are exploring “a more systematic approach to support QPs in keeping pace with evolving regulatory requirements”. This could include closer monitoring of the quality of QP submissions to regulatory agencies, as well as efforts to develop QPs’ competencies through relevant programmes.

Tembusu Grand , Arup, DP Architects among BCA award winners

Achievements in the BE sector were also celebrated at the event, with BCA presenting five projects and two companies with the PoY and CoY awards, respectively.

The PoY award honours projects that demonstrate a strong commitment to advancing Singapore’s BE industry. This year, Tembusu Grand won for the residential category, while the Pasir Ris 8 -Pasir Ris Mall integrated development won in the mixed-use category.

Other project winners include Bulim Square for the industrial category, Outram Secondary School (Sengkang Campus) for the institutional category, and Subsea Water Pipeline Tunnel Connecting Tuas and Jurong Island – Contract 1 for the infrastructure category.

For the CoY awards, global consultancy firm Arup and construction company Woh Hup emerged as winners for the large firms category, while DP Architects won for small firms.

BCA also presented the Quality Excellence Award, which recognises developers and builders for their commitment to delivering high-quality private residential buildings and implementing world-class industry standards.

City Developments won for the developer category, while China Construction (South Pacific) Development Co and Woh Hup were winners in the builder category.

title: We Analysed the Biggest Investing Mistakes Investors Make During Bull Markets
article:
Everyone seems to be making money during a bull market run.
Rising share prices, however, can give investors a dangerous boost of confidence, leading them to believe good times never end.
The biggest risks may not necessarily come from the market but from the mistakes investors make when prices continue to rise.
Mistake #1: Chasing Stocks After They Have Already Rallied
A common folly is this: “It keeps going up, so I should buy before it is too late!”
Often, when stocks gain attention for their rise, they have already rallied.
If you are to buy a rising stock, make sure it is backed by strong earnings and durable competitive advantages, not optimism and hype.
DBS Group Holdings Limited
(SGX: D05) has been on a roll since April 2025, rising from S$38 per share to S$76.65 as of 4 September 2026.
The bank posted a record high of S$3.08 billion in net profits for 2Q2026, up 9% year-on-year (YoY), with its wealth management fees rising 42% YoY to S$919 million.
As Singapore’s largest listed company, DBS has seen its rally backed by strong earnings growth, healthy balance sheets, and future potential.
Mistake #2: Becoming Too Confident After a Winning Streak
Investors tend to
take on unnecessary risks
when previous trades worked in a bull market.
They load up their portfolio with similar stocks, hoping to replicate the success.
However, investment returns are not always repeatable.
Market conditions eventually change.
A concentrated portfolio can suffer disproportionately during a correction.
A portfolio consisting only of bank stocks like DBS,
OCBC Limited
(SGX: O39), and
UOB Limited
(SGX: U11) can suffer when there are sudden, rapid rate cuts.
Hence, investors should regularly review their portfolio allocations, especially in a bull market where positions can quickly become overly large.
Mistake #3: Ignoring Valuation
Great companies can become poor investments at the wrong price.
Valuation
is essential in determining expected returns.
A company’s price-to-book (P/B) ratio shows value relative to net assets, and its price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio measures growth potential.
The ratios are useful for comparing companies within the same industry, not companies in different industries.
When measuring valuation for
real estate investment trusts
(REITs), we look at metrics like yield, distribution per unit (DPU) growth, price-to-NAV, and leverage.
Asia’s largest listed REIT,
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust
(SGX: C38U), announced a 7.1% YoY increase in DPU to S$0.0602 for 1H2026.
With an aggregate leverage of 37.4%, CICT’s debt maturity profile remained well staggered, with an average term-to-maturity of 4.1 years, helping to mitigate refinancing risk in any single year.
Mistake #4: Selling Good Investments Too Early
Bull markets can tempt investors to lock in gains prematurely.
However, even if the profit looks large now, selling strong businesses early can reduce long-term returns.
Instead, ask yourself before selling:
Are earnings still growing?
Is the competitive advantage intact?
Is management still allocating capital well?
Is valuation still reasonable?
If the answers are yes, holding onto the
winning stock
might be a better choice.
Mistake #5: Forgetting That Bull Markets Eventually End
During a market rally, it is easy to build a portfolio that only works when prices rise.
It is common to underestimate the importance of diversification, balance sheet strength, sustainable dividends, and free cash flow when everything is rosy.
Build a strong portfolio with diversified businesses: defensive consumer staples such as
Sheng Siong Group
(SGX: OV8), which has zero debt; strong, reliable banks such as DBS; and global technology and defence groups such as
Singapore Technologies Engineering Ltd
(SGX: S63).
The goal is not to predict exactly when a bull market ends, but to own investments that can withstand different market conditions.
What Bull Markets Teach Investors
Discipline matters more than hype.
Long-term success depends on fundamentals, not emotions.
Investors should be asking themselves these questions:
Am I buying because the business is good or because the stock price is going up?
Am I taking on unnecessary risks?
If the stock price falls by 30%, would I still hold the business?
How to Invest When the Market Keeps Rising
Stick to your investment process and keep evaluating businesses using the same criteria.
A strong market does not mean you need to stop investing.
However, it does call for you to be more selective with what you buy.
Focus on opportunities where valuations remain reasonable.
Maintaining diversification across sectors and companies is also essential.
Investors should rebalance their portfolios by reducing positions that have become overweight, but without liquidating their holdings due to a rise in prices.
Above all, keeping a long-term outlook is very important.
Market corrections are inevitable.
A well-constructed portfolio can weather different market conditions and still aid you in long-term wealth creation.
How Different Investors Can Respond
New investors do not have to feel pressured to “catch up” in a bull market.
Start with a sensible, diversified portfolio.
You can look at
blue-chip stocks
and REITs as a starter.
Do not chase winners just because they are winners.
Experienced investors should check if their portfolio risk has increased during the market rally and re-evaluate valuations.
Check if the initial thesis for each holding is still valid.
For income investors, it is important to pay attention to the sustainability of dividends and not simply go for high yields.
Business quality remains important.
Dividends should be paid out of sustainable earnings and free cash flow, not debt.
Get Smart: Don’t Let a Bull Market Change Your Process
Bull markets are exciting.
They can create wealth but also make investors abandon the habits that built their wealth in the first place.
Chasing fads, being overconfident, disregarding valuations, and taking unnecessary risks will make you vulnerable to changing market conditions.
The smartest investors ensure that their portfolio continues working for them under new conditions.
Strong markets are the time to review your investment strategies, not abandon them.

title: Adnoc said to be in talks for Thailand, Dangote refinery stakes
article:
(Sept 7): Abu Dhabi National Oil Co is in talks with the biggest refining companies in Thailand and Africa to invest in their businesses as it looks to secure customers for its crude and expand fuel trading, according to people with knowledge of the situation.

The Abu Dhabi company is seeking a stake in refineries run by units of Thailand’s PTT Pcl in a deal that would include contracts to supply crude and give Adnoc access to fuels from the facilities that it would then sell to other buyers, according to the people, who asked not to be named discussing private deliberations. A deal could be announced later this year, they said.

Adnoc is also in talks with Nigeria’s Dangote about taking stakes in its refinery operations, according to the people. The company founded by billionaire Aliko Dangote operates Africa’s largest refinery in Nigeria and is also planning to build a facility in the continent’s east.

Dangote has received approaches from many large players, said a senior executive at the company, who declined to comment on Adnoc specifically. Adnoc and PTT didn’t respond to requests for comment.

Building an international refining business is a change of strategy for Adnoc, with the company so far relying on its Ruwais facility at home, one of the world’s largest processors, to supply fuels globally. But it’s now considering deals as part of a plan to secure buyers for its own and other crudes, and to bolster its trading business. The war in the Middle East that’s upended supply through the Strait of Hormuz has also highlighted the importance of expanding operations outside the Persian Gulf.

Overseas refinery deals would add to Adnoc’s multi-billion-dollar international push, following unit XRG’s transactions for natural gas assets from the US to Africa and Central Asia, and the acquisition of German chemical-maker Covestro AG. Subsidiary Adnoc Distribution in July agreed to buy Shell Plc’s fuel retail operations in South Africa.

See also: Fuji Offset Plates Manufacturing moves ahead with RTO of Marco Polo's yards

Its closest competitor among Middle Eastern oil producers, Saudi Aramco, already has substantial investments in international refining, notably the giant Motiva facility in the US and stakes in several Chinese plants that allow the Saudi company to boost oil exports to the Asia’s biggest economy.

For Adnoc, Thai refineries that use heavier crudes could be a good fit for oil grades from Abu Dhabi’s offshore fields, the people said. Adnoc’s trading arm could also buy crude produced by other countries, such as Iraq, to supply those refineries, they said.

Adnoc is also interested in entering the downstream market in India, where it has previously struggled to gain a foothold. In 2018, the company piggy backed onto a Saudi Aramco deal to buy a stake in India’s Reliance Industries Ltd’s refining business, but talks never led to a transaction.

See also: Nvidia deal with Hugging Face makes billionaires of French co-founders

A potential east African refinery deal could also include stakes in a crude oil pipeline connecting the planned refinery in Lamu to Kenyan oil fields in the north, according to the people familiar with the talks. Adnoc has previously purchased African crude, including Nigerian barrels, for trading and has sold fuels like gasoline and diesel to countries including Kenya and Ethiopia.

title: IREIT Global secures 25-year lease for its Berlin property
article:
IREIT Global has secured a 25-year lease agreement with Berlin’s main public transport operator for its revamped property that is now called Berlin RE(0 Campus.

Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe, or BVG, as the tenant is called, will take up 39,419 sqm of this property for use as its headquarters.

The transaction represents the largest office letting in Germany thus far this year, and the largest office letting in Berlin since 2020.

Terms of the leasing agreement allow for a fixed 2.25% annual rent escalation, thereby supporting long term growth for the REIT.

Now, this tenant will move in only via four phases starting from Oct 1 2028 to Sept 30 2030, with the 25-year lease expiry from the date of the last handover.

IREIT is bearing the cost of fitting out the space for this new tenant. There is also a 12-month rent-free period at the start of each of the four phases.

See also: Beyond Singapore: Unpacking Keppel DC REIT’s $1.39 bil Tokyo acquisition

This lease agreement is on top of two earlier 20-year leases with hospitality businesses Premier Inn and Stayer.

With BVG's tenancy, the committed occupancy rate of the Berlin RE(O Campus will improve "materially" from 25% to 75%.

The remaining 18,000 sqm of available space is currently being actively marketed to prospective occupiers, providing further potential to build on the leasing momentum achieved to date.

See also: Multi-year high yield differential between S-REITs and banks could prompt ‘switch’ back into S-REITs: DBS

"Securing BVG as a long-term anchor tenant is a landmark achievement for IREIT and a defining moment in the transformation of our Berlin asset," says Peter Viens, CEO of the REIT's manager.

"This lease materially lifts occupancy, significantly enhances long-term income visibility and validates our repositioning strategy for Berlin RE(O Campus."

At the portfolio level, this lease will lift IREIT’s portfolio committed occupancy from 81.5% to 90.8% and extend its WALE from 6.7 years to 10.2 years.

IREIT Global units closed at 17 cents on Sept 7, up 1.82% for the day but down 44% year to date.

title: Thai sugar output to drop at least 17%, worsening global squeeze
article:
(Sept 7): Thailand’s sugar output may drop at least 17% in the coming season, adding to the strain on global supplies as dryness hits some of the world’s major growers.

Production is likely to fall below 10 million tonnes in the 2026-27 year that starts in October, according to Rangsit Hiangrat, the director of industry association Thai Sugar Millers Corp. That compares with 12 million tonnes in the prior season.

The country is the world’s second-largest exporter, and the downturn comes as the El Niño weather phenomenon strengthens — which is known for bringing dryness to swathes of South and Southeast Asia. The supply risks have pushed New York sugar futures higher, with prices climbing more than 20% last month in the biggest jump since 2010.

Rainfall in the northeast, which accounts for about 45% of Thailand’s total production, has been lower this year than in other parts of the country, Hiangrat said. In addition, relatively higher cassava prices could encourage local farmers to switch crops, he added.

In India, another major sugar grower, rainfall during the monsoon season that ends this month has also trailed normal levels. The International Sugar Organization forecasts a global deficit of about 260,000 tonnes in the coming season, citing El Niño’s impact on harvests in Asia.

See also: Palm oil climbs as Indonesian forest fires puts supply at risk

Thailand’s sugar output peaked in the 2017-18 and 2018-19 production years at more than 14.5 million tonnes, according to data from the Thai Sugar Millers Corp. Production has held lower since and typically averages about 10 million tonnes, produced from around 90 million to 100 million tonnes of sugarcane, Hiangrat said.

title: Zeiss overhauls SAP cloud migration after costs hit €200 mil
article:
(Sept 7): Germany’s Zeiss Group, a key supplier to the global semiconductor industry, overhauled plans to move to a new cloud-based SAP SE software service after costs swelled to more than €200 million over several years.

The precision optics maker will now use a so-called brownfield approach, which means moving its existing software systems to the cloud, in order to save money, according to people familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public.

External consultancies are leading the transition, the people said. The initial attempts to build a new system from the ground up were more complicated than expected, they added.

The decision offers a window into the complexity and expense of cloud transformations, a process that will drive SAP’s growth through the end of the decade. Starting in 2020, SAP CEO Christian Klein has pushed customers to move from locally hosted enterprise software to a subscription-based online service, which is more lucrative for the company and currently accounts for more than 60% of revenue.

SAP is Europe’s largest software company and sells products to manage finances, supply chains and other core business functions. More than 90% of the Fortune 500 use its solutions. Moving to the cloud can be a complex process and many customers still haven’t completed the transition, even as SAP plans to end regular support for its legacy on-premise solutions by the end of next year.

Cloud migration projects often involve external partners such as Accenture, EY or PricewaterhouseCoopers and take years and millions of dollars to complete. Moving sensitive business data is a delicate operation and can cause critical disruptions if done poorly.

See also: German industry output unexpectedly drops most in almost a year

US medical tech company Zimmer Biomet Holdings Inc sued Deloitte last year over a botched implementation of SAP’s cloud platform. The complaint alleges the process “was a disaster” and the result “was an overly customised software system riddled with defects and functionality gaps.” Zimmer paid US$94 million in fees, 36% more than Deloitte had represented, according to the complaint.

Deloitte is fighting Zimmer Biomet’s “meritless claim", according to a company spokesperson. A spokesperson for Zimmer Biomet declined to comment.

Zeiss began planning its path to the cloud six years ago and has now reconfigured the migration of its enterprise resource planning, or ERP, software “to achieve faster progress", a spokeswoman for the company said in a statement. She declined to comment on the investment or the project’s timeline.

See also: Economists see final ECB hike next week in split with markets

A spokesperson for SAP declined to comment on customers’ projects.

Zeiss is the exclusive supplier of optics used in ASML Holding NV’s most sophisticated lithography machines, which make advanced semiconductors, including for Nvidia Corp. Based in the German city of Oberkochen, Zeiss is expanding its operations to meet booming demand from chipmakers, the head of its semiconductor division, Frank Rohmund, told Bloomberg last month.

Zeiss initially planned a greenfield approach, which would have meant building the company’s core IT functions from scratch in the cloud, according to the people. Such projects seek to get rid of needlessly complex legacy processes and streamline systems.

The company has now pivoted to a brownfield approach that will preserve many existing data systems, according to the Zeiss spokeswoman.

The cost of moving to the cloud is highly variable, according to Byron Ford, a consultant at the Berkeley Partnership who works on SAP migrations. Greenfield projects generally cost at least 20% more than brownfield ones but can be twice as expensive, depending on factors such as which geographies are moving, the number of systems involved and the client’s own resources, he said.

A greenfield migration of several systems in a single country might cost £35 million to £40 million and a global project twice that or more, Ford added.

title: Shein’s value down US$5 bil, among HK’s worst post-IPO weeks
article:
(Sept 7): Shein Global Holdings Ltd has lost about US$5 billion ($6.33 billion) in market value since its initial public offering as it finished one of the worst opening weeks after a major Hong Kong listing, underscoring investor concerns over the fast-fashion retailer’s growth outlook.

Even after a 3.2% surge Monday, their first gain since the IPO, the shares closed 19% down from the HK$48.56 ($7.85) offering price. That’s the second-worst performance in the first five sessions among companies that raised at least US$1 billion in a Hong Kong listing, just behind a 19.9% plunge by Baidu Inc, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The company’s market value has dropped to about US$21 billion from roughly US$26 billion.

Completing a years-long listing process has done little to dispel concerns over Shein’s weakening profitability, regulatory headwinds and intensifying competition. Once valued at about US$100 billion during the pandemic-era e-commerce boom, Shein is now facing a much tougher environment, leaving investors sceptical about its ability to rekindle growth. The losses also highlight the limited appetite for traditional e-commerce businesses as capital is increasingly flowing toward companies involved with artificial intelligence and robotics.

“Shein’s decline reflects the growing market concerns of tariffs, fulfilment costs and execution risks surrounding its marketplace transition,” said Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Catherine Lim.

Lim said the sell-off was largely driven by company-specific concerns, though it also reflected broader scepticism toward cross-border e-commerce models amid tariffs, de minimis changes and tighter regulation. The shift towards AI and technology stocks has exacerbated the weakness, but questions over Shein’s growth and margins remain the key concern, she said.

See also: Chipmaker Longsys said to price Hong Kong listing at HK$236 — Bloomberg

Shein came to the public market as its once-rapid expansion was losing momentum. The company posted a loss of US$99 million in the first quarter, compared with a profit of US$395 million a year earlier. Revenue increased 8% in 2025, slowing from 21% growth in 2024 and falling short of the company’s target.

The weak performance adds to a rocky start for the retailer’s long-awaited listing after years of attempts to go public overseas. Once viewed as a pandemic-era growth champion, Shein is now grappling with slowing expansion, higher trade barriers and mounting competition in global e-commerce.

Shein’s debut foreshadowed the weak demand for the shares, which fell as much as 10% in early trading before a late-session rebound left them down just 0.1% at HK$48.50. The stock traded well below the offer price for most of the session before a late rebound narrowed the losses.

title: Eurozone growth upgraded after bumper quarter for Ireland
article:
(Sept 7): The eurozone economy expanded more than initially thought in the second quarter after a sharp upward revision in Ireland.

Gross domestic product increased 0.6%, up from a preliminary estimate of 0.4%, Eurostat said Monday. That’s the strongest quarterly pace in more than a year and comes after the 21-nation stagnated in the first three months of 2026.

The revision was triggered by Ireland, which said last week that output jumped by 10.2% between April and June. That’s up from an earlier reading of 3.9% thanks to a strong performance by multinationals that include Apple Inc and Eli Lilly & Co.

The economies of France, Austria and Portugal, on the other hand, all fared worse than initially thought.

See also: India says US trade deal hinges on preferential tariff rate

Despite inflation at a three-year high due to the Iran war and borrowing costs rising, the outlook is looking rosier for Europe as governments spend big on defence and infrastructure, and companies invest in artificial intelligence. Germany, the region’s largest economy, appears to be leaving behind a years-long malaise.

Eurostat’s data are the last major input for the European Central Bank before it sets interest rates on Thursday. Investors are betting on a quarter-point increase, a move officials will be more confident about knowing growth in the 21-nation economy is robust.

Analysts including Bantleon’s Daniel Hartmann now expect expansion of more than 1% this year, well above the 0.8% predicted by the ECB in June. Economists at JPMorgan, BNP Paribas and Societe Generale are among those who’ve recently added a hike by the ECB at year-end to their outlooks.

See also: China-US spat at G20 boils down to dispute over one word — Bloomberg

In the second quarter, trade and household spending were the main contributors to growth. Employment advanced by 0.1%.

title: Yen rises to highest since February, tops intervention rally
article:
(Sept 7): The yen strengthened to its highest level since February, surpassing the peak reached after coordinated intervention by Japan and the US.

Japan’s currency suddenly extended gains to rise as much as 1.4% to 154.06 against the dollar amid thin trading due to a US holiday. It had weakened to 160.39 last week.

“The yen’s break below 155 is significant given the level previously acted as a floor following past intervention episodes,” said Masahiko Loo, senior fixed income strategist at State Street Investment Management.

Growing bets on Bank of Japan interest-rate hikes have fuelled a sharp reversal in sentiment toward the yen after weeks of questioning the long-term effectiveness of the coordinated intervention by Tokyo and Washington. Speculation over a potential shift in the Government Pension Investment Fund’s asset allocation has also offered support to the currency.

According to State Street Investment Management’s Loo, a new month is typically accompanied by active real-money portfolio reallocation flows, which also appear to be supporting the yen.

See also: Won climbs to two-year high with rally momentum at extremes

Japan’s top foreign exchange official Atsushi Mimura said on Friday that there’s been no change in his fighting stance on the yen, a comment that came even as the currency strengthened against the dollar.

Chances that the yen could extend its recent gains were reflected in the options market. Volatility that captured the upcoming meetings by the BOJ and the Federal Reserve rose Friday to its highest level since January while the premium to hedge against yen strength stood near its cycle highs.

See also: Philippine peso slides past 62 against dollar as intervention risk grows

The break below 155 may prove significant as large stop-loss orders below the level were triggered and options dealers were forced to sell dollars as barriers were breached, adding to the yen’s gains, according to a trader familiar with the transactions who asked not to be identified because they aren’t authorised to speak publicly.

title: BlackRock, JPMorgan bet on EM as turmoil seizes global bonds
article:
(Sept 7): As government bonds from major economies buckle, funds including those run by JPMorgan Asset Management and BlackRock Inc have found an unlikely edge in emerging markets.

Government debt from the US to Japan has tumbled as energy-driven inflation and fiscal concerns revive the prospect of higher interest rates. Yet much of the developing world has escaped the worst of the selloff, helped by inflation that remains relatively contained, already-restrictive monetary policy and stronger fiscal positions in some countries.

High real interest rates and stronger fiscal positions in parts of the developing world are offering investors both income and a place to ride out volatility shaking the biggest bond markets.

The recent global bond selloff “makes EMs more attractive as they act as an income diversifier”, said Pierre-Yves Bareau, chief investment officer for emerging-market debt at JPMorgan Asset Management.

Local-currency emerging-market bonds have returned 3.6% this year even as US Treasuries and European peers have lost 0.6%, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The MSCI EM currency index has advanced for 11 straight weeks, its longest stretch of gains since 2007, and hit another record high on Monday.

See also: Indonesia set to boost cash placed in state banks to US$22 bil

“It speaks to the asset class’s resilience,” said Elina Theodorakopoulou, a portfolio manager for emerging-market debt at Manulife Investment Management, who sees the recent selloff as “a relative opportunity for global emerging market debt”.

In contrast with developed market peers, emerging-market central banks have more room to chart their own course. Inflation across developing economies is running at an average 3.8%, according to JPMorgan, roughly a third of the level during the 2022 shock. The bank estimates policymakers have about one percentage point more cushion to absorb price pressures than they did four years ago.

That flexibility is already on display. Brazil, Turkey and Hungary cut borrowing costs in August while South Korea and the Philippines tightened. The Czech central bank held rates after raising them in June.

See also: MAS June survey shows expectations of growth moderation and higher inflation

“With inflation still contained and growth close to or slightly below potential in a number of EM economies, local rates should also be relatively well anchored in the face of the developed-market bond selloff,” said Chris Kushlis, chief emerging markets macro strategist at T Rowe Price. His team favours local-currency bonds in Brazil, Hungary, Mexico and South Africa.

Similarly, Michel Aubenas, BlackRock’s chief of emerging markets debt, is targeting bonds where he expects central banks to surprise investors by leaving rates unchanged.

BlackRock, like Societe Generale, favours Czech markets on the assumption that policymakers will not be pressed into raising rates. Market pricing indicates one 25 basis-point hike by the end of this year for a total of 100 basis points by mid-2027 but SocGen expects the Czech central bank to hold rates at 3.75% for the foreseeable future.

SocGen strategist Juan Orts also contends that market bets for the National Bank of Poland to unleash three quarter-point hikes are overblown.

“The market is always too aggressive,” said Bareau at JPMorgan, whose funds favour local-currency bonds and speculative-grade sovereign debt. “Even if some central banks will hike in front of inflation, they won’t deliver all the premium that the market is pricing.”

History also offers some encouragement. Emerging-market debt has typically performed well during Federal Reserve tightening cycles when higher rates are driven by stronger growth rather than inflation and fiscal stress.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Growth in emerging-market economies is expected to remain steady near 3.7% this year, a rate that’s helping shore up public finances and driving a favourable ratings trend in countries like Argentina, Ghana and Nigeria. By contrast, fiscal pressures are rising in big-spending governments in the developed world and driving up yields.

“The fiscal profligacy of developed markets in general makes EM more interesting,” said Thomas Christiansen, chief investment officer and head of EM debt at Union Bancaire Privee. “And to some extent, I believe that DM bond market moves over the past few weeks is a reflection of this.”

title: Huawei, Xiaomi to debut new top phones on eve of foldable iPhone
article:
(Sept 7): Huawei Technologies Co and Xiaomi Corp are raising the stakes in China’s smartphone arena just days before Apple Inc’s first foray into the foldable category.

Huawei on Monday will unveil the latest edition of its ultra-premium trifold device, the Mate XT 2, which has two folding mechanisms. The successor to the Mate XT released two years ago, this new device advances the complexity of engineering and combines a regular smartphone and a large-screen tablet into one. It’ll be the first to feature Huawei’s new LogicFolding chip design philosophy, as the company seeks novel ways to advance performance.

Later in the evening, the Xiaomi 18 Fold will mark another step from a Chinese manufacturer toward greater reliance on domestic suppliers. The new handset will run on memory from homegrown champion CXMT Corp. and Xiaomi’s self-developed Xring O3 processor. It also features a passport-like design that mirrors what the first foldable iPhone from Apple is expected to look like.

The defensive action from two of China’s top brands underscores the threat and opportunity that Apple’s entry into the niche but premium foldable segment represents. Expected to be priced at more than US$2,000, the foldable iPhone will bring new attention to these devices, which Chinese makers and global shipments leader Samsung Electronics Co have been selling for years. In China, foldables have been a resilient bright spot in an otherwise declining market.

“Apple has the world’s biggest premium device installed base. Its foldable will sell well and rapidly grab market share,” Counterpoint analyst Ivan Lam said. He expects the new handset to spur wider adoption among consumers, with spillover effects that also lift demand for rivals’ devices as well.

Xiaomi’s profit has declined for three consecutive quarters as the company worked to reduce shipments of unprofitable low-end devices. Huawei, though still posting shipment growth, also saw its profit decline in the first half this year in part because the company was forced to hoard more components to fend off rising memory costs. Huawei joined Xiaomi and Honor Device Co in a fresh round of price hikes earlier this month, local media Jiemian reported.

See also: Abu Dhabi’s G42 weighs US ownership to safeguard AI chip access — Bloomberg

Smartphones are headed for their worst contraction on record this year, with shipments likely to decline 14%, Counterpoint data shows. Chinese smartphone makers are among those worst hit due to their outsize exposure to budget devices that are least able to digest the cost of surging component prices. To escape that crunch, most brands are now heavily promoting the premium segments, such as foldables, in order to raise their average selling prices.

Getting out a couple of days before Apple’s splashy new product event on Wednesday gives brands the chance to own the spotlight at least momentarily. Apple could grab a quarter of the global foldable market this year and claim the No.1 spot with a 41% market share next year, according to projections by Smart Analytics Global.

title: SGX Equity Derivatives Monthly Highlights Aug 2026
How Singapore and Malaysian Investors Can Access the Thai Stock Market
article:
Thai equities have recently been gaining attention
as renewed foreign investment flows and improving investor sentiment have helped the market outperform several regional peers.
With Thailand nearby, it’s no surprise that Singaporean and Malaysian investors are taking a closer look at Thai stocks. From
consumer products to industrials, services, and resources,
the Thai market offers exposure to companies across a diverse range of sectors for investors looking to expand beyond their home markets and explore new opportunities.
A Crash Course on Thailand’s Stock Market
The
modern history of Thailand’s capital market
began with the privately owned Bangkok Stock Exchange and later progressed with the establishment of the
Securities Exchange of Thailand.
The Securities Exchange of Thailand, renamed the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) in 1991, plays a key role in mobilizing capital to support Thailand’s economic and industrial development. After marking its 50th anniversary in 2025, the SET continues to strengthen the country’s capital markets and expand investor access. The
Market for Alternative Investments (MAI)
, a separate market operated by the SET, provides access to smaller and growing companies.
The
SET Index
tracks the performance of all common stocks listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand. Across the SET and MAI,
more than 850 listed companies
were listed, with a combined market capitalization of approximately THB 17.4 trillion as of 2024. Together, these markets give Singaporean and Malaysian investors access to a broad range of companies, complemented by Thailand’s geographic proximity within the region.
4 Ways Singaporean and Malaysian Investors Can Access Thai Stocks
Option 1: Direct Investing on SET Through a Thai Broker
Directly investing in Thai stocks
may be more suitable for experienced investors because the process involves several administrative steps.
Investors typically need to select a Thai brokerage firm, choose between a cash account, cash balance account, or credit balance account, submit the required documents, and wait for the brokerage’s approval before they can begin trading. For non-resident individual investors, capital gains from selling exchange-listed shares are generally exempt from Thai tax, while dividends are generally subject to a 10% withholding tax. Investors should still check whether taxes apply in their country of residence.
Foreign investors should also understand how the type of security they purchase affects their rights. Foreign investors holding local shares are generally not entitled to dividends or voting rights. Foreign shares, identified by the “-F” suffix, provide financial and voting rights but are subject to foreign ownership limits. Non-Voting Depository Receipts, identified by the “-R” suffix, generally provide the same financial benefits as the underlying shares but do not carry voting rights.
Option 2: Use an International Brokerage
If you want to skip the process of opening a Thai brokerage account,
an international brokerage can offer a more convenient alternative
. Your existing Singaporean or Malaysian brokerage may already provide access to the SET, allowing you to manage Thai investments alongside your other holdings in one account.
However, this convenience may come with higher trading and transaction fees. Before getting started, check whether your brokerage offers direct access to the SET and compare the costs involved.
There are also several factors to consider, including currency-conversion costs and exchange-rate spreads, custody arrangements, market access, and regulatory protection. Understanding these costs and conditions upfront can help investors decide whether using an international brokerage is the right fit.
Option 3: Invest Through Thailand-Focused ETFs or Funds
Thailand-focused ETFs
and funds can provide diversified exposure without requiring investors to select individual stocks. Investors with access to the SET can purchase locally listed ETFs, while those without Thai market access may be able to find Thailand-focused funds listed or offered in other markets. ETFs typically track an index, asset class, or investment strategy and hold a basket of securities within a single fund.
As of September 2026, there are
13 ETFs listed on the SET
, covering a range of asset classes that include Thai equities, international equities, bonds, and gold.
However, ETFs come with risks that investors should understand, including declines in the value of their underlying assets and the possibility that an ETF’s market price may differ from its net asset value because of market supply and demand.
Option 4: Thai Companies Listed or Accessible Overseas
Lastly, investors can gain exposure to Thai companies through securities traded outside Thailand.
For investors with brokerage accounts that provide access to the SGX, including eligible Singaporean and Malaysian investors,
Singapore Depository Receipts (SDRs)
offer a convenient way to access selected Thai stocks without trading directly on the Thai market.
Similar to American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), SDRs trade on the SGX under the Thailand-Singapore DR Linkage and are designed to make selected foreign-listed companies, including Thai companies, more accessible. They allow investors to trade in Singapore dollars through the SGX using a brokerage account with the necessary market access. The SDR framework also represents an important step in strengthening cross-border market connectivity within ASEAN.
Diversifying Your Portfolio with Thai Stocks
Thai stocks have attracted renewed attention following a sharp market rebound. Thailand’s benchmark index had
gained approximately 30%
since the beginning of the year, marking a sharp turnaround from its performance in 2025.
For Singaporean and Malaysian investors, there are several ways to tap into Thailand’s emerging potential. Direct market access offers greater control but can come with more requirements, while ETFs, international brokerages, and overseas-listed securities can provide simpler alternatives.
Whichever route you choose, look beyond access alone. Consider the costs, currency risk, liquidity, regulations, and the investment itself should all be considered before committing capital.
